Information received since September indicates a still-strong labor market and moderate growth, but with a soft capex/export mix: household spending is firm while business fixed investment and exports remain weak. Evidence on investment and inventories (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein, 1994) links such weakness to financing conditions and internal funds, consistent with the Committee’s precautionary easing and its T-bill purchases/repo operations to keep reserves ample and money markets stable. With overall and core inflation below 2% and market-based inflation compensation low, New Keynesian estimates (Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido; Rudebusch) imply muted inflation when output gaps are modest and expectations are anchored (Svensson; Cagan). The rate cut to 1.5–1.75% and supportive operating tools should cushion real activity (McCallum & Nelson, 1999; Sims and Zha), but global uncertainties keep risks tilted to the downside. Net tone: cautiously positive on current conditions, mildly concerned about investment and an inflation shortfall.
